design_choice: Every requirement is a single question naming the decision it supports, its horizon and its last time of value, scored QIR = [S x D x F] x (R + T) on 1-4 scales
source: Thomas p115-120; Fleurat et al. ch6; Arici 2.1.1

design_choice: Each requirement decomposes into SIRs and EEIs, mapped to sources in a traceability matrix whose empty cells are the collection gaps
Every panel names the requirement it answers
Vector first, actor second: the Big 5 vectors plus a fraud lens, with identity and valid accounts as its own card under hacking

Threat = intent + capability + opportunity, each rated with its basis; theater and vector levels are inherent threat with no credit for mitigations, and residual risk sits on its own page, labeled as such
source: Tiepolo & Sorensen p42-43, p520; Thomas p178-183; AI-Enabled TI p23-24
where: Vectors page, Brief header, Residual risk page

design_choice: Residual risk = inherent (vertical-calibrated vector level) x exposure x (1 - control coverage); coverage is set with control owners, exposure comes from the organization's own scans and dark-web monitoring, and each bar states its exposure basis

Theater and vector levels are re-weighted per critical-infrastructure vertical, since escalation raises the probability and urgency of activity against specific sectors; the weights are a stated analyst lens and the base level stays visible beside the calibrated one
where: Header vertical selector; Map, Theaters, Vectors and Residual risk pages

design_choice: A world map shows the region and vector overlap at a glance: theaters placed and sized by calibrated level, countries shaded by theater level or leak-site claims, with the political environment one click away
Each theater pairs region and vector with a cyber nexus, sponsor posture, a postulated scenario and a 'so what'; escalation raises the matching requirement's priority
source: Thomas p71-72, p94-98; Tiepolo & Sorensen p60, p626

design_choice: Pages run perception, comprehension, projection; source health is the JDL level-4 loop
Leading indicators per theater with states not observed, emerging, observed, confirmed

A closed source registry with Admiralty reliability and default credibility, trust tier, owner type, validity, collection method, provider bias, maintenance class, time-field contract and seven feed criteria
source: Fleurat et al. ch5, ch7, ch8; Tiepolo & Sorensen p523-525; Thomas p149-152; Arici 7.1.1, 7.3.3; Skopik p286; Kuhn p66; Bhardwaj p169

design_choice: Adversary-controlled channels (leak sites, belligerent statements) are graded D or lower or credibility 3, shown as claims, and never stand alone
source: Fleurat et al. ch8; Tiepolo & Sorensen p524; Arici 2.2.1, 3.1.3

design_choice: Corroboration counts independent origins; syndicated copies of one origin count once
source: Thomas p232; Fleurat et al. ch2; Arici 3.5.3, 7.3.3; Ransomware Analysis p60

design_choice: Conflict arcs default to actor-to-action pairs that two or more distinct articles report; single-article pairs, the ones GDELT most often misplaces, appear only when the analyst asks for them
source: Thomas p232; Fleurat et al. ch2; Arici 3.5.3

design_choice: Veracity states for each item: claimed, reported, corroborated, confirmed, denied
source: Yang et al. (Demystifying AI/ML for CTI) p312-317

design_choice: Source health: freshness against each source's cadence and stale thresholds, taxonomy drift and blocked collection shown openly
source: Arici 3.5.1, 7.3.1; Kuhn p80; Fleurat et al. ch16

design_choice: The live layers read a collector that keeps each feed's last good state in its own store, checks every upstream every 30 minutes with 24-hour and 7-day uptime, and serves its stored document marked stale, with its age, when an upstream fails
source: Arici 3.5.1, 7.3.1; Kuhn p80; Fleurat et al. ch16

design_choice: Technical feeds are perishable: live claims, indicators and EPSS refresh in the browser on demand or on a typed interval, each feed's cache window is shown, and indicators appear as family counts to avoid indicator bloat
where: Header controls; Brief live panel; Vulnerabilities page

design_choice: Indicators on the map show defanged and count by family; the raw ip:port is one deliberate copy away for blocking, and every mark links to the feed's own record
Dark-web reads enter only as counts about the organization's own estate; adversary-controlled channels stay low-reliability unless corroborated, and credentials or personal data never reach the page
Severity and confidence are separate badges
Item score = reliability (A 1.0, B 0.8, C 0.6, D 0.4, E 0.2, F 0.3) x credibility (1 1.0, 2 0.8, 3 0.6, 4 0.4, 5 0.2, 6 0.3)

HIGH needs 3+ independent origins across 3+ evidence categories, a mean item score of 0.7 or more and an alternative considered; MEDIUM needs 2+ and 2+ with a mean of 0.4; otherwise LOW; attribution judgments cap at MEDIUM
source: Fleurat et al. App. A, ch9; Tiepolo & Sorensen p518, p526

design_choice: Each judgment carries an argument map, key assumptions with their if-wrong impact, alternatives, indicators of change and a what-if line
source: Fleurat et al. ch9-10; Arici 2.1.4; Tiepolo & Sorensen p510

design_choice: The executive page shows only MEDIUM or HIGH judgments, at most six, each with situation, assessment, an action line and a NIST CSF 2.0 tag
source: Thomas p212-215; Fleurat et al. ch11; Suryavanshi ch10; Automating CTI p328; AI-Enabled TI p24

design_choice: Likelihood uses ICD-203 estimative terms and stays separate from confidence
Priority follows a milestone ladder (published, PoC, weaponized, exploited, commoditized), then SSVC and the KEV deadline; CVSS is shown but never used alone
source: Automating CTI p342-344; Ransomware Analysis p85; Fleurat et al. ch13

design_choice: An edge-device lens over KEV with publication-to-KEV lag
source: Tiepolo & Sorensen p240-243; Kuhn p81; Fleurat et al. ch13

design_choice: Each CVE shows its data gaps (CVSS version, CWE, SSVC)
KEV is US-centric; non-US advisories are a separate planned lane
Actor rows carry motivation, playbook by tactic with gaps, software, campaigns and release changes
Attribution is quoted as the attributing source stated it; a second curator sits beside it and divergence is shown, never resolved by the page

Attribution arcs are off by default and labeled historical: they join an actor's attributed country to the countries the MISP galaxy cluster's CFR fields name as victims, quoted as the curators recorded them with their confidence, and never drawn as observed traffic
The ATT&CK release diff is treated as events; technique prevalence is counted across state nexus groups
Items (what a source reported) are stored apart from judgments (owned hypotheses)
The daily run is a harness: closed catalog, generator, judge, verifier, and a deterministic validator with final authority; fetched text is untrusted
The run ledger is hash-chained
Comments become FP-numbered follow-on requirements, classified and prioritised for approval
A standing blind-spot statement: open sources only, no internal telemetry or HUMINT, insiders barely visible, zero-days seen only after disclosure
source: Arici 3.1.2; Tiepolo & Sorensen p43-46; Thomas p145

design_choice: Survivorship caveat on leak-site counts and a media-share check against availability bias
A disruption lane for takedowns, sanctions and indictments as indicators of change
STIX 2.1 export of judgments with TLP and PAP; the product takes the most restrictive marking of its inputs

The map carries a live conflict layer: GDELT 2.0 event exports, armed actors only, CAMEO material-conflict events, shaded by country against a 48-hour baseline with an anomaly ratio, plotted as conflict-event cells with an hour window and playback, and listed as the most-reported events, so the region and vector overlap updates between daily runs
source: Thomas p94-98; Tiepolo & Sorensen p626; Skopik p275-282

design_choice: Maritime oil-transit chokepoints are plotted with EIA-sourced crude and product flows, each tied to the theater whose escalation threatens it, so a geopolitical level reads against the trade it puts at risk
source: U.S. EIA World Oil Transit Chokepoints; Thomas p94-98

design_choice: Hostile infrastructure appears on the map as live layers: Feodo Tracker botnet C2, ThreatFox ip:port indicators, DShield top scanning sources and URLhaus malware hosts, placed by IP geolocation with each mark linked to its source record, beside IODA country-level internet disruptions; the page states that geolocation places the hosting rather than the operator

Replay re-runs the last 24 hours in the order the sources timed each record (feed first-seen times, GDELT export hours, IODA start times), and wall mode loops it as a situation display, so tempo reads from the timing the sources reported

Live exposure monitoring reads breaches (HIBP), leak-site listings that name the organization or a named supplier (ransomware.live) and egress-IP reputation (Tor Project, abuse.ch, GreyNoise) for the operator's own watchlist only, and reports counts and categories, never credentials

Technique priority is prevalence plus choke point plus actionability, each 0 to 1, the CTID Top ATT&CK Techniques method with its components recomputed per vertical from ATT&CK v20, this dashboard's threat model and current Sigma, Elastic and Splunk content; drivers are shown beside every score and a shift column compares the vertical's ranking with plain ATT&CK frequency
source: Thomas p202-206; Fleurat et al. ch13; CTID Top ATT&CK Techniques

design_choice: A group's weight in the threat model comes from its stated nexus theater at the vertical's calibrated ThreatCon, halved when neither ATT&CK nor MISP names one of the vertical's sectors as a target, or from a financial motive at the vertical's Ransomware or Fraud level; groups at 0.6 or more are in scope
source: Tiepolo & Sorensen p573, p626; Bhardwaj p142-143

design_choice: ATT&CK is read in reverse as a map of where public detection and test content runs out, weighted by threat use over leaf techniques; Reconnaissance and Resource Development are kept apart as activity outside the estate
where: Defense page: tactic coverage, blind-spot candidates, actor coverage

design_choice: Data components are ranked by the summed priority of the top 100 techniques whose ATT&CK analytics read them, the public half of a DeTT&CT visibility assessment; the organization's own visibility score per component completes it
where: Defense page: telemetry to collect first

design_choice: Each technique carries a hunt hypothesis in the template "Based on intelligence that X uses T####, we hypothesize..." with the data to scope, the queries to start from and the tests that validate it
Technique co-occurrence in CTID's report dataset suggests what else to look for after an observed technique and is labeled a hypothesis for the hunt; the intrusion's own evidence decides
source: Fleurat et al. ch13; Tiepolo & Sorensen p52
where: Defense page: what else to look for

design_choice: Purple-team test definitions record the behavior, its intelligence justification, scenario, telemetry, testable hypothesis and prevalence band; results use Detected-Alerted, Detected-Noisy, Detected-Late, Logged-Not-Detected or Missed with a content, telemetry or process root cause

The priorities and the public detection gaps export as ATT&CK Navigator layers scored 0 to 3 and 0 to 1, with each technique's drivers in its comment, so a group's layer can be combined with them by score expression
CRI Profile v2.1 diagnostic statements are ranked by the share of top-100 prevalence that the techniques each statement mitigates carry, using CTID's mappings carried to ATT&CK v20

Each exploited or early-warning CVE carries dated milestones (published, first public PoC repository, first Nuclei template or Metasploit exploit module, KEV listing); the race against KEV is measured only for CVEs published since KEV opened, and weaponized CVEs outside KEV are listed as patch priorities
source: Automating CTI p340-345; Ali & Bhatti p175-178; Fleurat et al. ch13

design_choice: Warning indicators that a live feed can measure carry analyst-set rules, marked direct or proxy; a theater's tempo counts independent collection families, so GDELT and Lanes count once, and a proposed state change waits for the analyst
where: Theaters page: measured indications and warning
